Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

Hey! Your PR title `chat.model hook` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #49908: OpenCode V2 cannot access OpenCode Zen free models — same root symptom (V2 beta builds cannot use Zen free tier models)
- #49756: Free tier zen models fail due to missing/incorrect headers forwarded to the Zen API — closely related root cause (client version/identity not properly sent)
- #49433: "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" error — same free-tier access failure, different version context

If your issue is distinct (specifically the `0.0.0-beta-*` version string causing the `1.18.0 or newer is required` check to fail), it may still be worth keeping open as a separate tracking issue, but please check those first.

Checked the three issues named in the duplicate note.

#49908 is the same outcome: OpenCode 2 cannot call Zen free models. Its text attributes that to unsupported Zen authentication headers, and it records no version, HTTP status, or reproduction. This issue measures a different error: `opencode2` `0.0.0-beta-19059` and `0.0.0-beta-19271` return HTTP 426, `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`, while `opencode` 1.18.31 returns the assistant text for `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`. If the failure behind #49908 is this 426, this report is the reproduction for that issue. The header explanation in #49908 is a separate claim.

#49756 is a different failure. It uses stable OpenCode 1.18.31, `opencode serve`, and HTTP 403 with `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`. The report says the server omits `User-Agent`.

#49433 is a different failure. It uses `opencode` 1.3.17 and the same 403 `can only be used from within OpenCode` message, not the 426 version check and not OpenCode 2.

Yes, I only had one workspace. I added another one while trying to figure out what is going on. I've clicked into the workspace. Gone across all tabs. The Settings tab included. The Billing section is where the "Invoices" are. There is an invoice for $20 there. Zero balance. There is literally NO HISTORY on the account. No usage, no logs, nothing if I click the "..." on my account name (you) in members and go through those pages. My keys are there. Everything else is blank.

**Data point on your #32656 warning: on 1.18.31 the cap did not bite us, even though we are exactly the profile you said would.**

Current config (since 2026-09-15, opencode 1.18.31): model declares `{ context: 262144, input: 240000, output: 32768 }` — output well above the 20,000 figure you cited — with `compaction: { auto: true, prune: true, tail_turns: 2, reserved: 50000 }`.

Measured from our session DB (context size of the last assistant request before each auto-compaction part):

- without `limit.input` (June–August): firings at 229,862–242,813 — branch B, consistent with both reports here;
- with the config above (firings 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-17): 190,396 and 199,989 — i.e. `input − reserved = 190,000` plus normal turn overshoot. If the branch-A `COMPACTION_BUFFER = 20_000` cap from #32656 were active here, the expected firing point would be ~220,000 (`240000 − 20000`).

So on 1.18.31 `reserved` appears uncapped for us: either #32656 was fixed between 1.18.21 and 1.18.31, or its trigger conditions are narrower than described. Worth checking which, since the workaround recommendation in this thread depends on it.

Your other two points both match our experience:

1. **Stale server config:** yes — our `limit.input` workaround did nothing until the server restarted; `opencode debug config` showed the resolved values, which misled us into thinking the file-level fix had taken effect.
2. **UI percentage desync:** confirmed — the indicator never approaches 100% after the workaround, which is how we first noticed something was off.

**The 2026-06-09 report in this thread (binary `webfetch` response → session DB poisoning) is still a live failure mode, and I think the auto-close buried it.**

The title's hang symptom is one issue, but the data-corruption path is a distinct bug with a clean repro: fetch a URL that returns binary bytes (PDF/image/archive) → raw bytes are written into the session log → every subsequent API call replays the binary and the provider rejects it → the session is permanently unusable and must be deleted. Our workaround (a fetch tool that validates Content-Type and blocks binary signatures + prompt guardrails) is still load-bearing because of this.

Suggestion: if this issue stays closed on the hang side, the corruption path deserves its own issue — happy to file a fresh one with the repro if maintainers agree.

This issue might be a duplicate of several existing issues reporting the same Go usage calculation discrepancy. Please check:

- #47614: Weekly usage quota stays maxed at 100% even after the monthly billing cycle resets
- #43023: Go quota inconsistency — monthly usage percentage exceeds weekly percentage with mismatched cost statistics
- #41206: Go weekly/monthly quota does not match usage history
- #43032: Go plan monthly usage percentage doesn't reconcile with actual spend or weekly percentage
- #38855: Weekly usage limit reported as exhausted while rolling 5h limit never reached
- #42985: Go quota usage appears ~4x higher than displayed model cost

If your issue isn't covered by any of the above, feel free to keep this open and add any distinguishing details.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #50202: Big Pickle (Free Stealth Model) Produces Corrupted, Non-Functional Output — reports the same CJK/language drift and garbled output symptoms with the Big Pickle model
- #49800: Zen streaming output token-merge corruption on opencode/big-pickle — reports non-ASCII leakage, token-merge glitching, and corrupted output from the Big Pickle model's streaming path, which may explain the symptoms attributed here to the bash tool IPC layer

Since you noted the corruption stopped after switching models, the root cause may be server-side (Big Pickle's streaming/generation), rather than the bash tool's IPC pipe. The existing issues above track that angle. If you're able to reproduce the bash tool corruption consistently with a different model, that would help confirm whether this is a distinct client-side bug.

Data point on **v2.0.12**: this does not appear to be Firefox- or mobile-specific.

Testing the same server with Playwright, the plan/build selector is absent in **all three engines at all widths** — Chromium 153, Firefox 155 and WebKit each return **0** matching elements at both 1440×900 and 402×874 (iPhone-class viewport), with no console errors in any of them.

Agent switching does still exist, but only as the `agent.cycle` command (`packages/app/src/composer/commands.tsx:66`), which requires a keyboard — so on touch devices there is no reachable way to switch agent at all.

Might be worth retitling away from "mobile Firefox", since the desktop Chrome case behaves the same.

(Separately filed #50459 for a mobile-layout issue found while testing this — below 768px the "Add project" control is absent from the DOM.)

Thanks. I reviewed the related issues, especially #41391, #42985, #41206 and #43149.

I now understand the proposed quota-normalization logic discussed there:

`normalized quota usage = visible model cost × (60 / model Usage limit)`

So, for example:

- a model with a $60 monthly Usage allowance has a 1× factor
- a model with a $30 allowance has a 2× factor
- a model with a $15 allowance has a 4× factor

I also understand why it is possible for Weekly Usage to be 100% while Monthly Usage is around 50%:

- weekly shared limit: $30
- monthly shared limit: $60

Therefore, approximately $30 of normalized usage would result in:

- Weekly: 100%
- Monthly: 50%

So that part of the dashboard is understandable.

However, my actual concern remains: **I cannot reconcile my exported token usage with the approximately 51% monthly quota usage shown by the server.**

My exported CSV contains only 103 Go requests:

- 77 × Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor
- 16 × Grok 4.7
- 10 × DeepSeek V4.1 Flash

All rows have:

`billing_source = go`

The CSV contains approximately:

- 2.79M input tokens
- 35.62M cache-read tokens
- 200K output tokens
- 140K reasoning tokens

I tried recalculating the usage using the currently published model prices and the model-specific quota normalization described in the related issues.

Even when accounting for Grok's smaller Usage allowance and therefore its higher quota multiplier, I cannot reproduce anything close to the ~51% monthly quota displayed on my account.

Using the published pricing and current model allowances, my estimate is roughly in the ~18–20% monthly range.

I also tried deliberately conservative assumptions against my own case, including:

- treating Grok requests as long-context / higher-priced where applicable
- accounting for reasoning output
- using less favorable DeepSeek pricing
- applying a smaller DeepSeek Usage allowance instead of the temporary promotional allowance

Even under those assumptions, I get roughly ~34% monthly usage, still materially below the 51% shown by the server.
